Definition: from G331; to declare or vow under penalty of execration:--(bind under a) curse, bind with an oath.
BiblicalUsage: This is the verb of binding oneself under a curse. In Acts the Jews bind themselves with an oath to kill Paul before they eat, and in Mark Peter begins to curse and to swear that he does not know Jesus. Both times the curse is a man's own doing, laid on himself to make his words stick.
TheologicalSignificance: A verb for swearing a curse on oneself carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning, that men will call down God's judgment on themselves rather than tell the truth.
